entries.clue: Westminster's initial anger at Chuck's invasion of privacy (7)

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to chuck someone under the chin is to tap it lightly

annotation.surface: Westminster fumes at some politician called Chuck for snooping into private lives.
annotation.walkthrough: Chuck looks like a man's name; it is the verb, as in chucking a child under the chin.
annotation.definitionFit: A wiretap is a concrete instance of the abstract phrase: a secret listening device on a phone line, the classic way of intruding on someone's privacy.

entries.clue: (& 25dn.) Labour – I say! – operate smoothly (4)

blocks.note: 'Well!' and 'I say!' are both exclamations of surprise

annotation.surface: A cry of surprise that the Labour Party is running smoothly for once.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour has a capital only because it opens the clue; the party is a disguise for plain toil. The answer is split, with WELL entered at 25 down.
annotation.definitionFit: Here 'work' is used of a machine functioning, and 'well' supplies the manner, so the phrase is a plain two-word synonym for running without a hitch.

entries.clue: Calm about lust? F-off! (7)

indicators.note: off = gone bad, as milk goes off, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone told to calm down about their lust replies with a rude brush-off.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'F-off' look like a single expletive; split it and the F joins LUST as letters while 'off' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: a restful place or mood is a calm one, free of agitation.

entries.clue: An African people voices disapproval at independence (5)

blocks.note: tuts = clicks the tongue in disapproval

annotation.surface: A nation grumbles at the arrival of independence.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the language of African independence movements to hide a simple two-part build.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Tutsi are one particular ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi, so 'an African people' names the class they belong to.

entries.clue: Mock shag, sport? (4,3)

blocks.note: both are vulgar slang for sex

annotation.surface: A sly question about whether a pretend romp counts as sport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mock' reads as an adjective (a fake shag), but it is the verb. Shag is British slang for sex.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom matching a single verb: 'poke fun' needs 'at' in use, just as 'mock' takes an object, and both mean ridicule.

entries.clue: Ex-PM stifling ultimately frail constitution (6)

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so HEATH closes round the letter
ultimately = at the very end, so the last letter

blocks.note: last letter of frail, placed inside HEA…TH

annotation.surface: A former prime minister suppresses a weak constitution, political or bodily.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pushes 'constitution' toward the political document; here it is a person's physical make-up.
annotation.definitionFit: The bodily sense of constitution, as in 'a strong constitution', is a person's physical condition, which is their health.

entries.clue: No problem getting 'ayes' to switch, vegetable-like? (4-5)

indicators.note: switching the letters puts them in a new order

blocks.note: like peas, a made-up adjective, pea-sy

annotation.surface: A parliamentary vote where the ayes flip as easily as vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: PEASY is not a real word: the setter invents it as 'like peas' to complete the childish rhyme.
annotation.definitionFit: A playground rhyming phrase that works as an exclamation, just as 'no problem!' does, both saying a task is trivially simple.

entries.clue: Religious doctrine into Lego construction? That's sweet (7)

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other
LEGO bricks are rebuilt into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone builds a religious idea out of Lego bricks and finds it sweet.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lego is not a toy here but four letters to rebuild, with ZEN slotted in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a lozenge is one kind of sweet, a small flat tablet often medicated for a sore throat.

entries.clue: Said to be an evil character's skin (4)

indicators.note: said = spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Mr Hyde, Dr Jekyll's evil other self

annotation.surface: A villain's skin is described by rumour.
annotation.walkthrough: Mr Hyde is the monstrous side of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story; his name and an animal's hide sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym, used chiefly of animals: a hide is the thick skin of a cow or deer, especially once tanned into leather.

entries.clue: Reveal fun's ruined – getting past it (6)

indicators.note: ruined letters are broken and rebuilt

annotation.surface: Someone admits that getting old has spoiled all the fun.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of fun's is 'is', a joining word; the definition sits alone at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: The figurative sense: as a folded thing is opened out to show what is inside, a plan or story that unfolds is revealed.

entries.clue: Tries out another parliamentary session? (5)

indicators.note: out = in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A question about MPs trying out an extra sitting of Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tries out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning tests; split it and 'out' works on TRIES.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on the exam retake: Parliament 'sits', so a second sitting is jokingly a re-sit, which the question mark flags.

entries.clue: Quite impressive to be described so in the bed department? (4-5)

definitions.text: described so in the bed department?

blocks.clueFragment: described so in the bed department?
blocks.note: a furniture store's label for the largest standard double bed

annotation.surface: A saucy boast about someone's performance in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed department is a furniture store's; the surface wants it to mean something ruder.
annotation.definitionFit: King-sized means larger than usual, hence impressive; and in a bed shop it is the literal size label for the biggest beds.

entries.clue: Fellow gets on edge, with female cutting off Starmer's thing? (4-8)

blocks.note: the lip of a cup is its edge
to lop is to cut off

annotation.surface: A satirical dig at Keir Starmer, with talk of edges and cutting off.
annotation.walkthrough: Starmer, the Labour leader, is often accused of changing his positions; the question mark flags a definition by satirical example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by jibe: flip-flopping means repeatedly reversing policy, which critics claim is Starmer's habit.

entries.clue: Adorable, getting hot inside airplane escape device (5)

indicators.note: inside = within, so the piece sits within the other word

annotation.surface: Something sweet heats up inside an aeroplane.
annotation.walkthrough: The escape device is the inflatable slide passengers use to leave a plane in an emergency.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a chute is any slide, and the inflatable evacuation chute is the one on airliners.

entries.clue: Politician has to go after second lie (5)

indicators.note: after = following, so this piece is written second

blocks.note: a Tory is a Conservative politician

annotation.surface: A politician is forced out after a second lie is caught.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has to go' sounds like a resignation; it only places one piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism: 'telling stories' is the nursery way of saying telling lies, so a story is a fib.

entries.clue: Remains House leader, having sold out – touching (5,2)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
out = in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A leader of the Commons clings to power despite having sold out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House leader' and 'sold out' read as politics; one gives a single letter, the other four letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: someone who keeps a grip and does not let go stays put or persists, as 'remains' does, in the same third-person form.

entries.clue: Stage effects ultimately not working – resigns post (5,4)

indicators.note: ultimately = at the very end, so the last letter

blocks.note: a stage in a process is a step
a computer that is down is not working

annotation.surface: A theatre show's special effects fail and someone quits over it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stage effects' reads as theatre; split it and stage is a step, while effects gives only its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom of leaving office: someone who steps down gives up a position, as one who resigns a post does.

entries.clue: Face crumpled, etc in a manner of speaking (7)

indicators.note: crumpled letters are crushed into a new shape

blocks.note: dial is old British slang for face

annotation.surface: A face creases up, and so on, in a manner of speaking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' is a stock phrase meaning 'so to speak'; the answer takes it literally.
annotation.definitionFit: The stock phrase read literally: a dialect is a regional way of speaking a language, so it is a manner of speaking.

entries.clue: Go easy on the killing, macho Putin-style (7)

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them
go easy on it = have less of it

annotation.surface: A plea to Putin to ease up on the killing, delivered in his own swagger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top less' is an instruction to kill less, read as one word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: Putin is famous for bare-chested photo shoots on horseback, so going topless is his macho style.

entries.clue: Electronic group in favour of crack at end of day (7)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a crack or a dig is a gibe

annotation.surface: A band that favours a wisecrack at the end of the day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack' pulls toward breaking or drugs; here it is a wisecrack.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: The Prodigy were a British electronic dance band of the 1990s, known for 'Firestarter'.

entries.clue: Tax leads to Severn Trent downfall (6)

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Severn and Trent
rain is a downfall from the sky

annotation.surface: A levy brings down Severn Trent, the English water company.
annotation.walkthrough: Severn Trent is a water company in the English Midlands, which makes the rainfall pun fitting. 'Tax' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense: to tax something, like patience or resources, is to put strain on it.

entries.clue: Ex-PM given fine, London area (7)

annotation.surface: A former prime minister is handed a penalty in a London district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty to pay; it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Mayfair is one particular district, the expensive one in London's West End.

entries.clue: Complaint: mostly paltry drugs (7)

indicators.note: mostly = most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: MEASLY = paltry, without its last letter
E = ecstasy, so Es are ecstasy tablets

annotation.surface: A grumble that the drugs on offer are feeble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble; it is an illness.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example using the medical sense of complaint, an ailment: measles is one such infectious illness.

entries.clue: Hard to crack poor morale? Put your member in this (7)

indicators.note: H breaks into the letters like a crack
poor = in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A smutty suggestion for cheering up flagging spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: The member is an arm, a limb, not what the surface wants you to think.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: member means limb, and an armhole is the opening in a garment where you put your arm.

entries.clue: Political doctrine involving Macron in vest, with switch of direction (12)

indicators.note: involving = entangling, so the letters are mixed up
one compass point, N, is swapped for another, S

blocks.note: the N of MACRON (north) becomes S (south)

annotation.surface: A political doctrine embodied by President Macron in his vest, changing course.
annotation.walkthrough: N and S are both compass directions, so switching direction swaps one for the other before the letters are mixed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: conservatism is one political doctrine, the belief in preserving traditional institutions.

entries.clue: Slinky type loses head for a time-waster (5)

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a SIDLER, one who sidles, without its S

annotation.surface: A slinky character is beheaded for wasting time.
annotation.walkthrough: To sidle is to slink along sideways, so a slinky type is a sidler.
annotation.definitionFit: An agent noun matched to a phrase: an idler is someone who idles away hours doing nothing, so a waster of time.

entries.clue: see 1dn. (4)
Provocative once inside Sally's skirts (4)

indicators.note: inside = within, so EX sits within the other letters
a word's skirts are its edges, so its outer letters

blocks.note: outer letters of Sally, split S…Y

annotation.surface: Something provocative that used to be under Sally's skirts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like clothing; it means the edges of the word Sally.
annotation.definitionFit: The sexual sense of provocative, deliberately arousing, is what sexy means of clothes or behaviour.

entries.clue: Real idiot prepared to be leader (9)

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new order

annotation.surface: A real fool is lined up to take charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants a political leader; it is the newspaper kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A British newspaper term: the leader, or leading article, is the editorial giving the paper's own opinion.

entries.clue: Capital university: "Grabbing balls is immoral" (5)

indicators.note: to grab is to hold in the hand, so LSE holds OO inside it

blocks.note: London School of Economics, split L…SE
two round Os look like balls

annotation.surface: A university in the capital issues a statement condemning groping.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital is London, and its university here is the LSE.
annotation.definitionFit: The old moral sense of loose, lax in behaviour, as in 'loose living', makes it a synonym for immoral.

entries.clue: Acting powerless, being a lover (6)

indicators.note: P = power, so powerless drops the P

annotation.surface: A lover acting as though they have no power.
annotation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for power.
annotation.definitionFit: Crude slang: to lay someone is to have sex with them, so laying is taking the part of a lover.

entries.clue: MP's face-to-face with constituents when cuts likely to be made? (7)

definitions.text: when cuts likely to be made?

blocks.note: a British MP's regular drop-in session where voters bring their problems

blocks.clueFragment: when cuts likely to be made?
blocks.note: an operation, where a surgeon cuts

annotation.surface: A pun on MPs meeting voters while spending cuts loom.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's cuts are budget cuts; the answer's are a scalpel's.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: in Britain an MP's surgery is a constituency advice session, and surgery is also an operation, where incisions are made.
